title: What I'd take from it, and what changes for software

checks.text: The stance chip on every row. You see my recommendation ("Looks right", "Use B", "Unsure") without opening the card. On our board you open each one to find it.
"I'd go with X" with its basis. A tag says what the pick rests on: Evidence (tested, measured) or Unsure. We should add Judgement for taste calls.
"Then the agent will…" under each option, shown before you pick. Our act line is written for me; this one is written for you.
One Handled state, with Undo. This replaces our decided/done split, as the Flex brief asked.
↵ takes my pick only when I'm sure. On an Unsure card it does nothing, so you have to look. That's our look-closer rule, enforced by the keyboard.
L: look where I'm unsure. One key takes you to the evidence. For software, that's the file and line, or the before/after pair.
The send drawer lists what the agent has committed to, in order. That's where the owed list (below) begins.
The footer shows what the agent is doing: "Live · read 09:01", "Flex isn't open", "The agent is waiting on your answers. Last: …". This is the per-project agent state I suggest, already designed.

Media becomes software media. Waveforms and storyboards become before/after screenshots (Flip suits a UI change), diffs, test runs, and our walkthrough films, where Flex's timecoded notes fit as they are.
"Open in Flex" and "note at Flex's playhead" become "Open in the running app" through Switchboard, with the note pinned to the URL or screen you're on.
A film's seven stages become a project's phases, and the journey rail becomes the phase strip.
Flex has no overview and no record, because a film is about fourteen cards over a day. A project runs for months, so those two are ours to add.

body.html: Most of what I proposed in round one is already in the prototype, built and working: review mode, one Handled state, answers sent straight to the agent, a commitment list, agent status, live arrival. That moves the question from "what should it be" to "what does a project need that a film doesn't": the overview, the Record, several projects at once, and Switchboard.
